source_name: Ljubljanski potniški promet (LPP) – Urbana city card and Urbana app news
source_subtype: transit operator news + scheme product pages
why_relevant: Urbana is Slovenia's flagship closed-loop transit payment scheme; LPP publishes the migration to open-loop bank-card acceptance on buses, new validators, Bluetooth contactless validation and card top-up in the Urbana app. Ticketing acceptance is a leading indicator for contactless/open-loop rollout nationally.

source_name: Javni holding Ljubljana (JHL) – sporočila za medije
why_relevant: Parent holding of LPP and other Ljubljana utilities; issues the formal PDF press releases behind Urbana app/payment announcements and other municipal-utility billing changes. Useful because the PDF releases are more detailed and more archivable than the operator news snippets.

source_name: Slovenske železnice – Potniški promet: ticketing, kartomati and payment terms
source_subtype: transport operator terms + ticketing pages (sl and en)
why_relevant: National rail operator documents accepted payment instruments on trains and at self-service ticket machines (cash, bank cards, and notably Flik), plus the general terms for kartomati. A concrete, dated record of A2A instant-payment acceptance spreading beyond retail into transport.

source_name: IJPP – Integrirani javni potniški promet (national transport smartcard scheme)
why_relevant: Operator of the national IJPP chip card used across bus and rail. The scheme portal describes card issuance, subsidised-ticket flows and the data linkages behind them — the reference point for any move from closed-loop chip cards to open-loop bank-card acceptance in Slovenian public transport.

source_name: Big Bang – e-commerce payment announcements and marketplace seller terms
why_relevant: Leading Slovenian consumer-electronics retailer and an early adopter on the acceptance side: online Flik payment, crypto acceptance via GoCrypto, and a marketplace whose seller terms name Mangopay as PSP. Merchant terms documents are one of the few public places where the acquirer/PSP relationship is actually disclosed.

source_name: Lidl Slovenija – corporate site and Lidl Pay in-app payment
why_relevant: Lidl has introduced in-app contactless payment ('Lidl Pay') covering stores and EV charging, and the group has been an early merchant adopter of Wero in other markets — making it a bellwether for whether pan-European A2A wallets reach Slovenian grocery acceptance. Its Slovenian newsroom/app pages are the primary record.

source_name: HOFER Slovenija (ALDI SÜD) – corporate site / news
why_relevant: One of the largest Slovenian grocery chains by transaction count and a frequently quoted merchant on cash-versus-card mix. Its own communications cover self-checkout rollouts and digitalisation of sales systems, both of which drive acceptance-hardware and acquiring demand.

source_name: EasyPark Slovenija – municipal parking payment rollouts
why_relevant: Parking is a high-frequency, card-on-file acceptance category. EasyPark's Slovenian pages plus the accompanying municipal announcements document which payment instruments are accepted (Visa, Mastercard, Diners, PayPal) and which of 30+ Slovenian towns have switched from coin parkomati to app payment.

source_name: Mestna občina Ljubljana / MojaObčina.si – municipal payment-service announcements
why_relevant: Municipalities are large payment-accepting entities and publish dated notices when a new payment channel goes live (parking apps, transport, utility counters). MojaObčina.si aggregates the same notices across many municipalities, making it an efficient way to detect acceptance changes in smaller towns that never reach national media.

source_name: Marprom (Maribor) – parking and transport payment leaflets/notices
why_relevant: Maribor's transport and parking operator; publishes leaflets and notices on cashless parking payment and its own transit ticketing. Represents the non-Ljubljana municipal acceptance layer, which is systematically under-covered by national sources.

source_name: Tehnozvezdje – Slovenian consumer-tech trade blog covering retail payment launches
why_relevant: Consistently the first Slovenian outlet to write up merchant-side payment launches (Petrol's new payment/charging card, Mercator mobile payment, Lidl's phone-payment solution) and often adds critical operational detail (checkout throughput, user education) absent from the merchant's own release. Good early-warning and cross-check layer.

source_name: Monitor.si and Računalniške novice – Slovenian IT trade press on wallet/POS launches
why_relevant: Long-running Slovenian IT publications that cover merchant wallet launches (e.g. Mercator M Pay) and app-based transit payment with more technical specificity than general news. Useful for reconstructing historical timelines of acceptance-side rollouts back over a decade.

source_name: Slovenian national news outlets as merchant-payment quote sources (24ur, N1, Siol, Svet24, Metropolitan, Delo/Slovenske novice)
why_relevant: National media routinely obtain direct statements from retailers (Hofer, Mercator, Spar) about cash-versus-card and mobile-payment mix that the retailers never publish themselves, and they cover legislative proposals on mandatory cash acceptance. Tag/keyword pages act as ready-made topic feeds.

source_name: Trgovinska zbornica Slovenije (Slovenian Chamber of Commerce and Trade)
why_relevant: The retailers' collective voice on payment-acceptance costs, cash-handling obligations and interchange/merchant-fee policy. Acts as a pointer to which merchant issues are live and which member companies to track, and is the counterparty quoted in cash-acceptance legislative debates. Its member directory is a ready-made actor map for this cell.

source_name: AJPES – JOLP public register of annual reports for Slovenian companies
why_relevant: Non-listed merchants in this cell (Spar Slovenija, Hofer, Lidl Slovenija, Tuš, Big Bang, Mercator subsidiaries) do not publish investor communications, but must file annual accounts with AJPES. This is the only systematic route to financial scale and, in the notes, occasionally to payment-cost and receivables disclosures for those buyers.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – payments market analysis and strategic initiatives (merchant/acceptance dimension)
why_relevant: The central bank's payments-market analysis quantifies acceptance-side behaviour — merchant card acceptance, consumer willingness to use cards where loyalty programmes exist, cash access — providing the denominator against which individual merchant announcements can be sized. Complements, rather than replaces, merchant primary sources.

source_name: Tuš (Engrotuš) – Tuš klub app and retailer communications
source_subtype: retailer corporate site / loyalty app pages
why_relevant: Third major Slovenian grocery chain; its Tuš klub loyalty programme has moved to an app holding digital cards and push offers, the standard precursor to in-app payment. Needed for complete grocery-acceptance coverage alongside Mercator, Spar, Hofer and Lidl.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Pritožbe uporabnikov finančnih storitev (complaints against supervised entities)
why_relevant: Central bank page describing the formal complaint channel against banks, savings banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions, payment system operators and credit intermediaries. Defines the legal complaint taxonomy (ZPlaSSIED, ZPotK-2, ZVPot-1, ZPPDFT-2, ZCKR, ZSJV) that structures all downstream complaint statistics.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Letna poročila (annual reports incl. consumer-protection/complaint chapters)
why_relevant: Annual reports carry aggregate counts and themes of consumer complaints and supervisory actions against banks/PSPs — the closest thing to an official complaint-volume time series in Slovenia.

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) – Izvajalec izvensodnega reševanja potrošniških sporov (IRPS/ADR for banks)
why_relevant: ZBS is the recognised out-of-court consumer ADR body for Slovenian banks. Its ADR pages and annual reports disclose case volumes, dispute subject matter (unauthorised payment transactions, card fraud, fees, credit) and outcomes — a direct read on where banks fail their customers.

source_name: Zveza potrošnikov Slovenije (ZPS) – consumer advice, market reviews and bank-fee comparisons
why_relevant: Slovenia's main consumer association. Publishes named-bank market reviews (basic payment account availability, fee comparison tool used by Banka Slovenije), consumer Q&A on online payment abuse and bank refusals to refund — early indicator of recurring complaint patterns.

source_name: ZPS – Kam se obrniti, ko so kratene pravice potrošnikom (map of supervisory institutions)
why_relevant: Pointer page enumerating Slovenian supervisory/complaint bodies (TIRS, BSi, AZN, ATVP, IP-RS, ministries) — an actor map for the whole complaint-channel cell, useful for snowballing further sources.

source_name: Informacijski pooblaščenec RS (IP-RS) – GDPR/ZVOP-2 opinions (mnenja) including bank-specific ones
why_relevant: The Slovenian DPA publishes searchable non-binding opinions, many explicitly about banks (merger data transfers, employment data processing by banks, disclosure of client data between bank employees). These reveal where banks push data-processing boundaries and which systems are contested.

source_name: IP-RS – Varstvo osebnih podatkov / pristojnosti (inspection and sanction powers)
why_relevant: Explains inspection and complaint-decision powers under ZVOP-2/GDPR; the entry point for understanding what is and is not published about enforcement against banks and payment providers.

source_name: IP-RS – Katalog informacij javnega značaja (FOI catalogue; route to unpublished inspection decisions)
why_relevant: Inspection decisions (inšpekcijske odločbe) are reportedly NOT routinely published due to sensitivity, but are among the most-requested FOI items. This catalogue is the documented route to request specific decisions naming banks/PSPs.

source_name: OPSI – Praksa Informacijskega pooblaščenca (open dataset of DPA case practice)
why_relevant: Slovenian national open-data portal hosts the DPA's data-protection case practice as a machine-readable dataset — the most collectible form of DPA output for automated bank/payment keyword filtering.

source_name: Sodna praksa RS – sodnapraksa.si (Supreme/Higher/Administrative court case-law search)
why_relevant: Official case-law database covering SOVS/IESP/UPRS/VDSS. Contains rulings on unauthorised payment transactions, bank liability under ZPlaSS/ZPlaSSIED, online-banking security diligence, and consumer-credit disputes — litigation exposure signals that no bank press release will state.

source_name: Sodišče RS – Iskalnik sodne prakse (sodisce.si knowledge/case-law portal)
why_relevant: Judiciary's own portal into court decisions and court-level structure; useful pointer to per-court case databases and to Vrhovno sodišče decisions on banking disputes.
